elements.element: Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "The Company may assign this Agreement ... without HDI's consent, to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's prior consent
elements.evidence: "HDI may not assign or otherwise transfer this Agreement ... without the prior written consent of the Company"

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "(such consent not to be unreasonably withheld)"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and in no event to a competitor of the Company"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Original 10.3 and the redline contain no change-of-control termination right for HDI; condition demonstrably absent

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to a successor; HDI may assign with consent not unreasonably withheld (broader protection for us than mutual free successor assignment)
No notice obligation appears: "The Company may assign ... without HDI's consent"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "(such consent not to be unreasonably withheld)"

offending_extra_words: or of the business to which this Agreement relates
whether by operation of law or otherwise
Any purported assignment in violation of this Section shall be void.
reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent, Vendor assignment only with Customer consent (not unreasonably withheld), express competitor bar, and no Vendor change-of-control termination right (none existed to remove).

Minimality fails: the insertion goes beyond what the preferred position needs by adding 'reorganization', a business-line successor limb, 'in whole or in part', 'whether by operation of law or otherwise' and a standalone void-assignment sentence — unnecessary model-language boilerplate on top of the required operative terms.

The operation also re-states the entire trailing sentence as its anchor, driving the official ratio gates to fail; a separate concise insertion after the existing sentence would achieve the same result.
Intent is preserved: the original successors-and-assigns binding sentence remains intact, defined terms (Company, HDI) are used correctly, and no contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no written-notice mechanic), but that is irrelevant since preferred is met; note in the rationale rather than redlining further.
